speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a concerning rash and recent health changes; please tell me when these symptoms started and if you have any fever or other systemic symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned a new onset cough and recent arthritis management; has the rash appeared on your face or hands, and do you have any joint pain or swelling? Also, have you noticed any fever, shortness of breath, or changes in your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DRESS) likely secondary to recent initiation of arthritis medication, given the rash on the upper back, mucositis, new cough, and systemic involvement.
